answer: Proof-of-useful-work minting resists sybils: minting requires solving a genuinely useful externally-verified computation whose result has value, so the cost is real productive compute, not throwaway hashing. A timber-stack of fakes each needs its own full useful-work solve; the canyon of cost is the actual computation per identity, not amortizable. A zephyr of parallel hardware still pays per-identity useful-work cost, so a farm minting thousands performs thousands of real valuable computations — expensive at scale.
